mission: Gavran's archived note discovered — 'Ankhural theorized that the lattice could be reinforced through harmonic resonance between disparate traditions. We lacked the will or the trust to attempt it.' The seed of the climactic solution.
why_now: Deep in the archive data loaded from the fortress — Ben finds it while searching for counter-measures to Veraine's array
conflict: The note describes a theoretical solution no one has ever tested — and it requires exactly what the group lacks: trust between incompatible traditions. Ben notes it but doesn't understand its significance yet.
turning_point: Gavran's admission: 'We lacked the will or the trust.' The man who built the seal — the most powerful Jedi Lord of his era — couldn't do this. And Ben is supposed to succeed where he failed?
opening_hook: The note is buried in Gavran's personal annotations — marginalia on the Codex fragment, cross-referenced with a passage Ankhural marked as 'untested, requires conditions we cannot create.'
closing_hook: Ben bookmarks the note and moves on. He'll come back to it. He doesn't know yet that this is the most important thing he'll read on the entire journey.
emotional_trajectory: Discovery -> intrigued uncertainty -> filed away for later

stakes.personal: Ben holding the solution without recognizing it — dramatic irony for the reader
stakes.interpersonal: The note's requirement (trust between traditions) is exactly what the group is struggling to build
stakes.external: Chekhov's gun planted — the resonance theory will define the climax

setting: Aboard the Steady Returns — Ben's workspace, archive data on displays
sensory_details: Archive text in old script; Gavran's handwriting — precise but rushed; the note's passage highlighted against the Codex framework; Sera looking over Ben's shoulder, frowning at Ankhural's name
promises_planted: Gavran's note about lattice resonance will matter (PP10)
notes: H14 planted — the resonance note. Chekhov's gun. The reader should register this as important even if Ben doesn't yet. Sera's reaction to Ankhural's name is significant — she knew the scholar's reputation as a heretic.
